answer: Trust-flow conservation with per-node throughput caps resists sybils: trust propagates like a conserved flow where each node can pass only a bounded amount onward, so a chain of fakes cannot amplify trust as it relays. A reef of sybils relaying trust among themselves is throttled at each hop by the throughput cap; the lotus of honest trust spreads only as fast as genuine capacity allows. An ember of real seed-trust divided across a long sybil relay chain arrives attenuated and capped, so a bulk fake network cannot manufacture more standing than the conserved flow permits it.
